title: Baltic Sea anomaly: not attached to the seafloor, with electromagnetic activity

tellings.quote: Uh according to Dennis Aspx explorer who's a buddy of mine, uh it's not attached to the seafloor.

plain: A strange object on the bottom of the Baltic Sea is said not to be attached to the seafloor, and to show electromagnetic activity. Michels tells this himself, passing on what an explorer and friend of his named Dennis Asberg told him: 'it's not attached to the seafloor.' If true, it would mean the object is not a natural rock formation fixed to the seabed.
